To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
O-GlcNAclyation is an inducible, reversible posttranslational protein modification that is regulated by the availability of glucose and is a critical mediator of nutrient signaling.
OGT is an oncoprotein that drives the growth of breast cancer and other cancers by promoting the hyper-O-GlcNacylation of proteins that regulate cell growth and metabolism.
O-GlcNAcyclin (cycling between O-GlcNAylation and de-O-GlcNAcylated states) is a key nutrient-sensing mechanism that regulates cell growth, survival, and metabolism.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the mechanisms by which O-GlcNAcyclng enzymes sense and regulate changes in cellular metabolism, how this information is integrated with growth factor and oncogenic signaling to regulate cell growth, and how this information is used in the clinic to identify new therapeutic targets in cancer.
how nutrient sensing by O-GlcNAcation influences the expression of genes and the activity of enzymes involved in glucose and lipid metabolism and how this contributes to the pathogenesis of cancer.

how O-GlcNAcyclig enzymes sense changes in cellular energy levels and nutrient status to regulate the transcription of key metabolic genes, and how O-GlcNacylation of these transcription factors and metabolic enzymes regulates cellular metabolism and growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the O-GlcNAC modification of protein substrates represents a new and exciting area of cancer research.
the O-GlcNacylation of proteins is a critical regulator of cancer cell growth and survival.
the role of OGT in cancer is not well established and that the role of hyper-O-GlcNacylation in cancer is unclear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

O-GlcNAylation is a nutrient-sensitive, posttranslational regulator of cellular metabolism and growth, and that hyper-O-GlcNacylation is a key contributor to the development and progression of cancer.

the O-GlcNAC modification system serves as a nutrient sensor to integrate the availability of glucose, amino acids, and other nutrients into a single signaling pathway that regulates transcription, metabolism, and proliferation.
OGT is a tumor promoter and OGA is a tumor suppressor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
OGT is a key player in cancer cell metabolism.
protein O-GlcNacylation is an important regulator of the Warburg effect and that the Warburg effect is important for cancer cell growth.
the metabolic and transcriptional changes that occur during cancer progression are driven by the actions of the nutrient-sensitive protein O-GlcNacylation cycle.
